sourceContext: US UI/UX design agency; this page sells marketing website UX and UI design (structure, landing pages, CMS templates, Core Web Vitals) to marketing and growth teams.
abstract: UI UX web design covers the user experience (UX) and user interface (UI) of marketing websites: site structure, landing page design, responsive design and Core Web Vitals performance. Our UI UX web design engagement takes 4–8 weeks, costs $25,000–$60,000, and ends with Figma page templates ready for a content management system (CMS).

sections.h2: What is UI UX web design?
sections.answer: UI UX web design is the process of structuring, writing for and visually designing a marketing website so that visitors find information fast and take a clear next step. The work covers information architecture (IA), messaging hierarchy, page templates, responsive layouts and page speed.
sections.body: UI UX web design differs from web app design services in audience and purpose: a marketing website converts anonymous visitors, while a web app serves logged-in users who complete daily workflows. Website UX focuses on landing pages, navigation and forms; web app UX focuses on tables, permissions and multi-step tasks.

sections.h2: What does UI UX web design include?
sections.answer: Our UI UX web design services include 6 deliverables: a website UX audit, an information architecture, messaging wireframes, landing page designs, a responsive UI design and a CMS component set.

items.title: Website UX audit.
items.body: The current site is reviewed with Google Analytics 4 and Hotjar data, for example exit pages, scroll depth and form drop-off.

items.title: Information architecture.
items.body: A sitemap and navigation model are tested in an Optimal Workshop tree test, for example for top-level menu labels.

items.title: Messaging wireframes.
items.body: Low-fidelity wireframes set the messaging hierarchy of each page, for example headline, proof points and calls to action.

items.title: Landing page designs.
items.body: Conversion-focused templates cover paid and organic campaigns, for example product, pricing and demo-request pages.

items.title: Responsive UI design.
items.body: High-fidelity Figma designs cover 3 breakpoints, for example 375 px mobile, 768 px tablet and 1,440 px desktop.

items.title: CMS component set.
items.body: Reusable page sections map to Webflow, WordPress or Contentful, for example hero, feature grid, logo strip and FAQ blocks.

sections.h2: How does the UI UX web design process work?
sections.answer: The UI UX web design process takes 4–8 weeks (20–40 working days) and runs in 5 steps, from website UX audit to CMS handoff.

items.title: Audit and goals (3–5 days)
items.body: We review analytics, heatmaps and the current sitemap, and agree the conversion goals, for example demo requests or sign-ups.

items.title: Information architecture (3–7 days)
items.body: Designers build the sitemap and test navigation labels in an Optimal Workshop tree test.

items.title: Messaging wireframes (4–8 days)
items.body: Wireframes set the messaging hierarchy of every page template before visual design starts.

items.title: UI design and responsive layouts (7–15 days)
items.body: Designers produce responsive Figma designs that meet Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 level AA, for example 4.5:1 contrast for body text.

items.title: CMS handoff and launch QA (3–5 days)
items.body: We hand over CMS components, then check the built pages in Google Lighthouse against Core Web Vitals targets: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) under 2.5 seconds, Interaction to Next Paint (INP) under 200 ms and Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) under 0.1.

sections.h2: What are the benefits of UI UX web design?
sections.answer: UI UX web design has 4 benefits: it increases conversion rate, improves content findability, reduces page load time and develops a scalable page system.

items.title: Increases conversion rate
items.body: A clear messaging hierarchy and one primary call to action per page increase the share of visitors who request a demo or sign up.

items.title: Improves content findability
items.body: A tested navigation model improves how fast visitors find pricing, product and support pages.

items.title: Reduces page load time
items.body: Lightweight templates, compressed images and reserved image space reduce page load time and keep layouts stable on mobile.

items.title: Develops a scalable page system
items.body: Reusable CMS sections develop a page system that lets marketing teams publish new landing pages without a designer.

sections.h2: UI UX web design vs web app design
sections.answer: UI UX web design converts visitors on a public marketing website; web app design improves workflows inside a logged-in application. Companies with both a marketing site and a product run the 2 projects as separate engagements with shared design tokens.

sections.h2: How much does UI UX web design cost?
sections.answer: UI UX web design costs $25,000–$60,000 and takes 4–8 weeks. The price depends on 4 factors: the number of page templates, the number of landing pages, the depth of the IA work and the CMS platform.
sections.body: A website redesign with 6–8 page templates, 1 landing page and a Webflow component set sits near $25,000. A multi-audience site with 15–20 page templates, 5 campaign landing pages, a tree-tested IA and a WordPress or Contentful component set sits near $60,000. Online stores with category, product and checkout pages follow e-commerce UX design services instead.

sections.h2: When does a marketing team need UI UX web design?
sections.answer: A marketing team needs UI UX web design in 5 situations:
items: Demo requests stay flat, if website traffic grows month after month.
A rebrand launches, if the current website still carries the old messaging.
Visitors fail to find pricing or product pages, if the navigation grew without a plan.
Core Web Vitals fail in Google Search Console, if the templates load heavy images and scripts.
Marketing teams wait on developers for every page, if the CMS has no reusable sections.

sections.answer: These answers cover the 5 questions buyers ask most about UI UX web design.

faqs.q: Does UI UX web design include development?
faqs.a: No. UI UX web design delivers Figma templates and a CMS component set; the client's developers build the website.

faqs.q: Is UI UX web design different from web app design?
faqs.a: Yes. UI UX web design covers public marketing websites, while web app design covers logged-in applications with workflows, tables and permissions.

faqs.q: Can UI UX web design improve SEO?
faqs.a: Yes. UI UX web design improves search engine optimization (SEO) inputs, for example page structure, heading hierarchy and Core Web Vitals; content writing and backlinks sit outside the UI UX web design scope.

faqs.q: Which CMS platforms does UI UX web design support?
faqs.a: UI UX web design supports Webflow, WordPress and Contentful, with page sections designed as reusable CMS components.

faqs.q: How long does a website redesign take?
faqs.a: A website redesign takes 4–8 weeks, which equals 20–40 working days, from the website UX audit to CMS handoff.
